note: Searched all agent files for recovery, replay, retry, checkpoint, resume, audit reads, queues, idempotency and execution entry points, then traced app/loop.py, main.py, extractor.py, audit.py, approvals.py, gate.py, identity.py, mcp_client.py, ingest.py, startup.py, settings.py, budget.py, killswitch.py, context_size.py and every app/tools module, plus migrations, prompts, configuration, tests, release and deployment/CI files. Parent and extractor conversations are initialized in memory on each invocation; audit.py only inserts events and no application path reads audit_events to restore execution. Its tree-rebuilding comment describes audit reconstruction, with no executable recovery consumer. Persistent department notes and documents are business inputs, approval reads authorize newly proposed calls, quota reads enforce limits, and control flags halt execution; none restores a checkpoint or replays an action. Approval callbacks only update approval status, and the background task only expires approvals. ERP, Slack and payment clients issue single requests without recovery queues or retry loops; tool exceptions return an error rather than automatically resending. Payment idempotency keys are used during ordinary invocation. MCP notifications refresh tool metadata, and extractor results return directly to the current parent conversation. Startup and deployment recreate a service without loading prior runs. Model turns may propose another call, but there is no implemented automatic replay of a saved or failed action. Thus no logs or checkpoints drive recovery and no automatic replay was found; R14.1–R14.5 are inapplicable.
